newsitem.title: USA: Cerner says Q3 hurt by bookings.
newsitem.headline: Cerner says Q3 hurt by bookings.

text.p: Cerner Corp, which develops healthcare information systems, said Wednesday its third quarter results were hurt by failure of the company to meet its new booking objectives.
"Although sales activity has been and remains high, we simply have not closed as many agreements as we expected," president and chief operating officer Clifford Illig said in a news release.

But the company said it has increased the size of its sales staff and training resources, and has added a number of new marketing and communications programs to support the expanded sales force. Cerner also said it has completed the reorganization of the executive team responsible for sales and marketing.

Illig said the company's sales pipeline continues to grow, with interest in Cerner's Open Clinical Foundation Data Repository and market-leading departmental systems as well as Cerner's new Health Network Architecture (HNA) 500 platform.
"All of these factors should lead to an improvement in Cerner's bookings performance as we enter 1997," Illig said.

"Our revenue backlog stands at $198 million," Illig said. "We have a substantial base of recurring revenues from our existing client installed base which now exceeds $58 million annually, with a gross margin of over 75 percent."
The company has also slowed growth in operating expenses until it sees improvment in bookings, Illig said.
Earlier Wednesday, Cerner reported net income of $770,000, or $0.02 a share, for the third quarter, compared to $3.5 million, or $0.11 a share a year ago.
